## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

WatchRaceNavigator — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/WatchRaceNavigator.kt

## Trigger

Hilt constructing the singleton `WatchRaceNavigator` at app start-up,
via `NavigationModule.provideWatchRaceNavigator` — observed (it is the
same production call site that already supplies `sensorPermissionGranted`
and `profileAlreadySynced`).

## Today

`WatchRaceNavigator`'s initial value for `mutableCurrent` (read lazily
at `current`'s first access, per the class's own doc comment) is chosen
from `profileAlreadySynced` and `sensorPermissionGranted()` alone:
`HOME` if the profile is synced, else `SENSOR_PERMISSION` or
`WAITING_FOR_PHONE`. Nothing in the class, and nothing in
`NavigationModule.provideWatchRaceNavigator` (its sole production
caller), ever calls `RaceRecordingRepository.findInProgress()`. A race
that survives process death (per §7 of the conventions) is retrievable
— `MainActivity`'s `WatchApp` already reads `findInProgress()` in its
`MAIN`, `PROJECTION` and `CONTROL` branches to render it — but nothing
ever routes the user to one of those destinations on start-up; the
first destination is always `HOME`, `SENSOR_PERMISSION` or
`WAITING_FOR_PHONE`.

## Expected

`WatchRaceNavigator`'s first-read destination also accounts for a race
in progress: when one exists, it is chosen ahead of the
profile-sync/sensor-permission checks, so the app opens on the race
instead of `HOME`. `NavigationModule.provideWatchRaceNavigator` supplies
the check by calling `raceRecordingRepository.findInProgress()`, read
lazily at `current`'s first access — the same lazy-read discipline the
class already applies to `sensorPermissionGranted`, and for the same
reason: a race read taken eagerly at construction would not reflect
state written after Hilt builds the singleton.
